KEPLERS_LAWS.infoDialog.semiMajorAxis: Semi-major axis (a): represents half of the longest diameter of the elliptical orbit.
KEPLERS_LAWS.infoDialog.semiMinorAxis: Semi-minor axis (b): represents half of the shortest diameter of the elliptical orbit.

MODELS_OF_THE_HYDROGEN_ATOM.lInfo: {{l}}, the Angular Quantum Number, describes the shape of the orbital. Orbital shapes are spherical ({{l}} = 0 or {{s}}), peanut-shaped ({{l}} = 1 or {{p}}), and become more complex as {{l}} increases.
MODELS_OF_THE_HYDROGEN_ATOM.mInfo: {{m}}, the Magnetic Quantum Number, describes the orientation of the orbital in space.
MODELS_OF_THE_HYDROGEN_ATOM.models-of-the-hydrogen-atom.title: Models of the Hydrogen Atom
MODELS_OF_THE_HYDROGEN_ATOM.nInfo: {{n}}, the Principal Quantum Number, describes the electron's energy and its probable distance from the nucleus.
MODELS_OF_THE_HYDROGEN_ATOM.nlmInfo: The Schrödinger model uses 3 quantum numbers ({{n}},{{l}},{{m}}) to describe the most probable location of an electron, also known as an orbital.

MY_SOLAR_SYSTEM.unitsInfo.content: Note 1: An Astronomical Unit (AU) is about 150 million kilometers. This is the average distance between the Sun and the Earth.
MY_SOLAR_SYSTEM.unitsInfo.content2: Note 2: The mass values in this simulation range from 1 Jupiter mass to 1.5 Solar masses. All astronomical objects show a similar behavior under a strong gravitational field, including smaller planets, comets, and asteroids.
MY_SOLAR_SYSTEM.unitsInfo.content3: Note 3: Due to the large range of values in the simulation, the gravity force vectors may sometimes be too small or too large to display. The gravity force vectors can be rescaled with the zoom control.

QUANTUM_MEASUREMENT.averagePolarizationDialog.explanatoryPar: The equation yields a value between +1 and -1. This value represents a weighted average of the polarization of detected photons if each detection of vertical polarization is mapped to a value of +1 and each detection of horizontal polarization is mapped to a value of -1. This value can also be mapped to a vector representation that lies between the value of +1 and -1.
